raw_text:
Here’s a safe, progressive 12‑week general fitness program tailored to a 58‑year‑old male, six months post‑MI, cleared for moderate intensity only. Parameters honored: keep HR ≤70% age‑predicted max (≈115 bpm), avoid Valsalva and max lifts, emphasize controlled breathing, gradual progression, and symptom monitoring. Full gym available.

Global guidelines
- Intensity: RPE 3–5/10 (moderate). HR cap: ≤115 bpm. If meds blunt HR, use RPE and talk test (should be able to speak in full sentences).
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion, inhale on return. No breath‑holding.
- Tempo: 2–3 sec concentric, 2–3 sec eccentric, controlled range.
- Rest: 60–90 s between resistance sets; longer if HR approaches cap.
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min (5–6 min light cardio + mobility). Cool‑down: 5–8 min light cardio + stretching.
- Stop and report if: chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, palpitations, dizziness, excessive fatigue, BP red flags if available.
- Frequency target by Week 4+: 4–5 days/week (3 mixed cardio+strength days, 1–2 cardio/active recovery days).

Phases overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Reintroduction and movement quality. Build tolerance, establish HR/RPE awareness.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Volume build at moderate intensity. Introduce light circuits, gentle intervals within HR cap.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Progressive overload via sets/reps and low‑load complexity. Improve stamina and strength endurance.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Consolidation and variety. Slightly longer sessions or added low‑impact modalities while staying sub‑threshold.

Weekly structure (typical)
- 3 mixed sessions (A/B alternating): 45–60 min.
- 1–2 cardio/active recovery sessions: 20–40 min low impact.
- Optional short mobility on other days: 10–15 min.

Heart rate management
- Use continuous HR monitor if possible. Cap at 115 bpm; if exceeded, slow/stop until HR <100 bpm, then resume.
- Prefer steady, rhythmic modalities: treadmill walking, recumbent bike, elliptical without arms, rowing at gentle pace.

Week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 (Establish base, technique, tolerance)
Week 1 (3 mixed + 1 light cardio)
- Session A (full body, machines preferred)
  - Warm‑up: 5 min treadmill walk (flat) HR ≤100; Mobility: shoulder circles, ankle rocks, cat-cow x6 each.
  - Leg press (high seat, low load): 2×12 at RPE 3–4
  - Seated row (neutral grip): 2×12 RPE 3–4
  - Chest press (machine): 2×12 RPE 3–4
  - Supported split squat (bodyweight holding rail) or sit‑to‑stand from bench: 2×10/leg
  - Cable straight‑arm pulldown: 2×12
  - Standing calf raise (machine or bodyweight): 2×12
  - Anti‑rotation press (Pallof): 2×10/side
  - Cool‑down: 5–8 min easy cycle + gentle stretches
- Session B
  - Warm‑up as above
  - Recumbent bike: 10 min steady HR 95–110
  - Lat pulldown (wide‑to‑shoulder width): 2×12
  - Incline DB press (light): 2×12 (avoid breath‑holding)
  - Hip hinge pattern: cable pull‑through or light RDL with dowel: 2×10
  - Step‑up (low box, hand support): 2×10/leg
  - DB curl‑to‑press (very light, strict): 2×10
  - Side bridge (knees): 2×20–30 s/side
  - Cool‑down 5–8 min
- Session C (mixed cardio)
  - 5 min warm‑up walk
  - Treadmill walk 15–20 min, 0–2% incline, HR 95–110 (≤115)
  - Mobility circuit 10 min (thoracic rotations, hip flexor stretch, hamstring stretch, chest/lat stretches, 20–30 s each)
- Light Cardio Day
  - 20 min easy recumbent bike or pool walking HR 90–105 + 5 min breathing drills

Week 2
- Progress each resistance move to 3×10–12 at same RPE. Cardio segments +3–5 min total time if HR allows.
- Introduce gentle “mini‑intervals” on cardio: 2–3 rounds of 1 min at upper‑moderate (HR 105–112) alternated with 2 min easy, still ≤115.

Week 3
- Maintain 3×12 where form perfect; add one additional exercise per session for variety:
  - A add: Machine reverse fly 2×12
  - B add: Cable row to chest 2×12
- Cardio: 20–25 min steady or mini‑intervals 1:2 work:recovery. Keep total session ≤60 min.

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 (Volume and stamina)
Goal: 3–4 days/week consistent; introduce simple circuits to keep HR in moderate zone without spikes.

Week 4
- Session A (circuit, 2–3 rounds, 8–10 min/round, 60 s between stations as needed)
  - Leg press 12
  - Seated row 12
  - Chest press 12
  - Step‑ups 10/leg
  - Pallof press 10/side
  - HR check between stations; keep ≤115. RPE 4–5.
- Session B (steady cardio + accessory strength)
  - Recumbent bike 20–25 min steady HR 100–112
  - Accessory block: Cable pull‑through 3×10; Lat pulldown 3×10; Calf raise 3×12; Side bridge 2×30 s/side
- Session C (mixed)
  - Treadmill walk 5 min warm‑up
  - Elliptical (no arms) 10–15 min HR 100–110
  - Machine shoulder press (light, neutral grip) 2×10
  - Goblet box squat (light DB, box height so thighs above parallel) 3×8–10
  - Incline DB row 3×10
- Optional Session D: 20–30 min easy swim or bike HR ≤105 + mobility

Week 5
- Increase circuit rounds to 3 if HR allows; keep reps 10–12.
- Cardio: total weekly time +10–15%. Example: two 25–30 min steady sessions.
- Add gentle balance: tandem stance 2×30 s; single‑leg stand with support 2×20 s/leg.

Week 6
- Slight progression: choose 2–3 major lifts to add load 5–10% while staying RPE ≤5 and reps 10–12. Keep rest flexible to control HR.
- Cardio session include 4–5 mini‑intervals: 1 min HR 105–112, 2 min HR 90–100.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Strength endurance and variety)
Goal: Maintain submax intensity; progress via sets/reps, tempo, and exercise variations.

Week 7
- Session A (full body, 3 sets each)
  - Leg press 3×12
  - Chest press 3×12
  - Seated row 3×12
  - Split squat to bench 3×8/leg
  - Pallof press 3×10/side
- Session B (cardio focus)
  - Row erg 5 min very easy technique
  - Row 4×3 min at HR 102–110 with 2 min easy between; total 20–25 min
  - Mobility 10 min
- Session C (posterior chain + push/pull)
  - Cable pull‑through 3×12
  - Lat pulldown 3×10–12
  - Incline DB press 3×10–12
  - Hip abduction/adduction machines 2×12 each
  - Farmer carry light DBs 4×20–30 m, slow breathing, HR check
- Optional D: 25–30 min outdoor walk on flat path HR ≤110

Week 8
- Keep sets the same; introduce slow eccentrics on last 2–3 reps (3–4 s lowering) for leg press, rows, presses. Monitor HR/BP response.
- Cardio: one session with 6×1 min upper‑moderate (HR 105–112) with 2 min easy.

Week 9
- Circuit day reintroduced (3 rounds):
  - Step‑ups 12/leg
  - Chest press 12
  - Seated row 12
  - Goblet box squat 10
  - Cable face pull 12
  - Bike 3 min easy between rounds to maintain HR
- Total weekly cardio 90–110 min, split across sessions.

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Consolidate, small complexity bumps)
Goal: Slightly extend duration, reinforce adherence, prep for long‑term plan.

Week 10
- Session A (strength endurance, 3×12)
  - Leg press
  - Lat pulldown
  - Incline DB press
  - Split squat 3×8–10/leg
  - Pallof press 3×12/side
- Session B (steady cardio)
  - Elliptical or bike 30–35 min HR 100–112; cadence focus; nasal or pursed‑lip breathing
- Session C (machine mix + carries)
  - Chest‑supported row 3×12
  - Machine shoulder press (light) 2–3×10
  - Hamstring curl 3×12
  - Calf raise 3×12–15
  - Farmer carry 4×30–40 m (light)
- Optional D: 30 min walk + 10 min mobility

Week 11
- Maintain loads; add one set to two big moves (e.g., leg press and chest press to 4×10–12) if HR and RPE remain within targets.
- Cardio: include gentle hills on treadmill (1–3% incline) while monitoring HR; 30–35 min.

Week 12
- “Benchmark” week (submax, for comparison)
  - Cardio test: 30 min preferred modality at steady HR 100–110; record distance/average HR/RPE.
  - Strength sessions: keep same exercises, note RPE and HR responses. No increases this week.
  - Education: discuss ongoing plan: 2–3 strength days + 2 cardio days, total 120–150 min/wk moderate.

Exercise details and substitutions
- If any exercise elevates HR too quickly, reduce load, shorten set, or swap to a more supported machine variant.
- Favor machines/free weights that allow stable posture. Avoid floor‑down/up sequences if they spike HR.
- Core: prioritize anti‑rotation, side bridges, dead bug variations; avoid heavy bracing or high‑pressure moves.

Session template (for all resistance days)
- Warm‑up: 5–6 min light cardio + dynamic mobility (hips, T‑spine, ankles, shoulders).
- Main sets: 5–7 exercises, 2–4 sets of 8–12 reps, RPE 3–5, tempo controlled.
- Finisher (optional): 5–10 min easy cardio cool‑down.
- Stretching: calves, quads/hip flexors, hamstrings, chest, lats; 20–30 s each.

Breathing and blood pressure safety
- Cue exhale on exertion every rep; avoid breath‑holding.
- Seated/recumbent options for any dizziness.
- If available, pre/post session BP check; avoid training if resting BP >180/110 or symptomatic; stop if unusual symptoms arise.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: aim 7–9 h; consistent schedule.
- Daily walking: encourage 10–20 min easy walks on non‑gym days, HR ≤105.
- Hydration: 1.5–2 L/day, more if sweating.
- Stress management: 5–10 min/day of diaphragmatic breathing or mindfulness.

Nutrition (general, cardiac‑friendly; defer to physician/dietitian as needed)
- Emphasize Mediterranean pattern: vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, olive oil, fish 2–3×/week.
- Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day spread across meals to support muscle maintenance; select lean sources (fish, poultry, legumes, low‑fat dairy).
- Sodium moderation per medical advice; monitor if on diuretics.
- Pre‑workout: small carb‑dominant snack 60–90 min prior if needed (banana + yogurt). Post‑workout: balanced meal within 2–3 h.
- Caffeine/alcohol as advised by cardiology.

Progression rules
- Only progress one variable at a time (load, reps, sets, or duration).
- If HR reaches 115 or RPE >5, reduce intensity or extend rest.
- 2‑for‑2 rule (adapted): if for two sessions in a row HR stays ≤105 and RPE ≤4 with perfect form, increase load 2–5% next session.

Medication considerations
- If on beta‑blockers, rely primarily on RPE and talk test rather than HR alone.
- Bring nitroglycerin and follow cardiologist instructions if prescribed.

Check‑ins
- Weekly symptom review, recovery, sleep, and stress.
- Reassess after Week 6 and Week 12 to update targets.

This plan keeps intensity moderate, avoids Valsalva and maximal efforts, and progressively builds cardiovascular capacity, strength endurance, and confidence while honoring post‑MI safety.
